articles.headline: Fantasy football Week 10 inactives: Who's in and who's out?
articles.description: Updated inactives and analysis based on the latest reports and official announcements leading up to kickoff.
articles.body:
Biggest injury concerns for Week 10

Players in Germany

Amon-Ra St. Brown, WR, Lions (ribs): The "Sun God" was limited at practice this week and is listed as questionable but appears to be likely to play in Week 10. He played through the injury last week and surpassed 16 fantasy points. St. Brown, who is a German citizen, will look to put on a show.

A.J. Brown, WR, Patriots (ankle/knee): Brown has been limited at practice this week and was listed as questionable headed into Sunday's game. However, he is currently expected to play. Brown averaged eight targets per game for the two times that he played on over 75% of snaps. Given all the missed time, he brings some risk. Still, fantasy managers should probably take the chance here as Brown has a fantastic matchup against the Lions, who have allowed the fourth-most WR fantasy PPG.

Rhamondre Stevenson, RB, Patriots (knee): Stevenson was able to return in a limited fashion after missing practice to start the week. He is listed as questionable for Sunday, but is expected to play. He has a tough matchup against the Lions, who have allowed the second-fewest fantasy PPG. They rank bottom six in rushing touchdowns and rushing yards per game allowed to RBs. Assuming he suits up, he's a risky flex option. 

Hunter Henry, TE, Patriots (foot): Henry has been limited at practice this week but does not currently carry an injury designation for Week 10. That means he is expected to play. Henry is a TE1 worth starting against the Lions, who have allowed the most yards, touchdowns and fantasy points to tight ends.

Don't forget to check these out: Mike Clay's Playbook | Week 10 Buzz 

Week 10 Rankings | Matchup rankings for Week 10

Official Sunday inactives should begin coming in approximately 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff times: around 11:30 a.m. ET for the early games and 2:30 p.m. ET for the late-afternoon games.

Refresh often for the latest information.

Players with early starts

Harold Fannin Jr., TE, Browns (groin): While Fannin was limited at practice this week, he has been removed from Cleveland's injury report and will play in Week 10. The Texans' defense is tough on tight ends, having allowed the fourth-fewest fantasy PPG to the position. Still, consider Fannin to be a TE1 this week in a game where the Browns might be trailing and needing to throw.

Denzel Boston, WR, Browns (toe): Boston missed practice on Thursday before returning Friday. He is questionable for Week 10, but HC Todd Monken said on Friday that Boston is "trending in the right direction." On paper, Boston has a favorable matchup against the Texans, although they have been tougher as of late. He is in the WR3/flex range. If he were to sit, KC Concepcion gets the biggest boost and would be in a similar range as Boston. Fannin, albeit in a tough matchup, would also likely see a few more targets.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Arsenal eye former Tottenham striker Will Lankshear
articles.description: Arsenal are the latest team to join a long list of admirers following Middlesbrough striker Will Lankshear. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Arsenal are the latest team to join a long list of admirers following Middlesbrough striker Will Lankshear, while Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes is holding off on signing a new contract for now. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Arsenal are in the market for a center forward, and TEAMtalk claims that the Gunners are the latest team to join a long list of admirers following Middlesbrough striker Will Lankshear. The 21-year-old joined Boro from Tottenham Hotspur this summer, after a loan spell at Oxford United in the Championship, and has hit the ground running, scoring 13 goals in as many appearances in the league so far. That has brought about plenty of transfer interest, but Middlesbrough will try to block any exit in January.

- Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes is holding off on signing a new contract for now, says The Sun. Fernandes, 32, has a contract which expires next summer -- albeit with a one-year club option to renew -- and reportedly wants to wait to see what happens under new boss Mauricio Pochettino. The Portugal midfielder has been linked with a lucrative move to Saudi Arabia before.

- Arsenal are continuing the push to sign a left-sided forward, with RB Leipzig star Antonio Nusa leading their shortlist, says TEAMtalk. Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard left in the summer, and were replaced by Christos Tzolis before a move to sign Vinícius Júnior from Real Madrid fell short. With Mikel Arteta wanting more options on that flank, the report claims that talks have opened with Nusa's representatives about a possible switch, but the 21-year-old's transfer could cost €80 million.

- Tottenham defender Pedro Porro has decided that he only wants to join Barcelona if he leaves the club, according to Sport. The 27-year-old Spain right back has seen interest from the Blaugrana, as well as Real Madrid, despite only signing a new contract with Spurs in the summer. But while Barcelona are eyeing up a deal worth no more than €50 million next summer, Tottenham will stand firm on their €70 million valuation.

- AC Milan are looking to bolster in the forward areas during January, with Gazzetta dello Sport reporting that Real Madrid's Endrick and Club Brugge's Nicolò Tresoldi are on their shortlist. Endrick has seen few minutes in the starting XI for Los Blancos this season and Milan are keen on a loan deal with a permanent option included. Meanwhile, Tresoldi  22, who has five goals in four Champions League appearances this season, has caught the eye of a number of a teams and could move in a €60 million deal.

Other rumors

- Arsenal believe that Real Madrid forward Vinicius Junior will join the club eventually. (Football Transfers)

- Sunderland will look to block any move for Brian Brobbey, as Tottenham are eyeing a potential deal for the striker. (Football Insider)

articles.headline: Sources: Chiefs had renowned baseball doctors weigh in on Patrick Mahomes' elbow
articles.description: The Chiefs sought medical opinions from two renowned baseball doctors last week on Patrick Mahomes' injured elbow, sources told ESPN.
articles.body:
When it came to reviewing the scans of Patrick Mahomes elbow this past week, the Kansas City Chiefs covered all their bases -- literally.

In addition to their own doctors reviewing scans of Mahomes' elbow, the Chiefs branched out and had renowned doctors from the Kansas City Royals and Texas Rangers offer second and third opinions, sources told ESPN.

Doctors found that Mahomes suffered a muscle strain and also what one source described as "a very small sprain of his UCL."

All doctors believed that it was safe for Mahomes to resume playing, despite the fact that he was sore and continued receiving treatment throughout the week.

Now after a week of practice in which he took all the throws, Mahomes is expected to start Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons.

The Chiefs turned to baseball doctors because they felt those doctors deal with elbow injuries more in baseball than in football. The Chiefs knew that they could not send a $500 million player like Mahomes to just any doctors -- they wanted the best and brightest to examine the images of an elbow as valuable as Mahomes'.

The two individuals with deep ties to baseball that the Chiefs turned to were Dr. Vincent Key, the Royals' head team physician who specializes in Tommy John surgery and newer UCL repair techniques, and Dr. Keith Meister, the Rangers' team physician and orthopedic consultant, who is one of baseball's best-known orthopedic surgeons specializing in elbow and shoulder injuries.

Rick Burkholder, the Chiefs' vice president of sports medicine and performance, reached out to Key shortly after Kansas City's victory last Sunday over the New York Jets. Key reviewed the scans and, according to a source, felt like the Chiefs and Mahomes "got away with one." But he also recommended that another noted doctor review the images, and thus Meister was contacted Sunday night and offered a similar sentiment.

Both Key and Meister acted urgently and reviewed Mahomes' scans, and both agreed the two-time MVP suffered more of a muscle strain, according to sources, and that the damage could have been significantly worse.

Up until all the doctors had studied the scans and weighed in with their opinions, the Chiefs were concerned with what any one of them could find with Mahomes' elbow. They knew he stayed in the game, and how he has played through other assorted injuries in the past, but they worried about any damage they might find after it.

Just last week, Arizona Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew suffered an injury on a similar looking play to the one in which Mahomes was injured against the Jets.

Minshew suffered a torn UCL and is expected to undergo season-ending surgery, according to sources. He still is working on the timing of when to have the surgery, but he planning to have it.

articles.headline: Reaction as Brazil legend Ronaldinho comes out of retirement at Ravenna to chase 300th goal
articles.description: Ronaldinho is coming out of retirement to play for Italian Serie C side Ravenna at age 46 in a bid to score his 300th career goal. Here's how the world reacted.
articles.body:
Former Barcelona and AC Milan forward Ronaldinho, 46, will come out of retirement on Sunday to play for Italian Serie C club Ravenna against Forli.

The Brazil legend retired on 299 career goals, with his final match for Fluminense in September 2015, and he has chosen a third-tier club in Italy to try and reach the magic number of 300.

The club's 12,000-seater Stadio Bruno Benelli stadium has had an upgrade, with a temporary stand built to accommodate the growing interest in seeing the 2002-World Cup champion and back-to-back FIFA World Player of the Year winner play his final game.

Catch up on everything that happens during the game when it kicks off at 11.30 a.m. ET / 4.30 p.m. GMT.

articles.headline: Sources: Raiders planned to start Fernando Mendoza soon even if no Cousins trade
articles.description: The Raiders had a plan to start Fernando Mendoza in Week 12 against the Browns even if they had not traded Kirk Cousins, sources told NFL Network.
articles.body:
The Fernando Mendoza era likely would have begun soon, with or without the Las Vegas Raiders trading away Kirk Cousins.

Sources told NFL Network that the Raiders planned to unleash the No. 1 overall draft selection in the next few weeks even if Cousins had not been traded.

If Las Vegas had lost Sunday to the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks and the Denver Broncos on Nov. 22, Mendoza would have started on Nov. 29 against the Cleveland Browns.

The Raiders (4-5) always said publicly there was a plan for Mendoza, though they kept it private. This was the plan, especially if two consecutive losses meant the playoffs were an uphill battle.

It's all moot now, with Las Vegas trading Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings on Tuesday for a 2027 third-round draft pick.

Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Mendoza will have the entire playbook at his disposal, with the the organization believing the reigning Heisman Trophy winner works even more than they thought.

"His teammates know how prepared he is," Kubiak said. "It's not just lip service, but he has shown it on the practice field."

While there undoubtedly will be growing pains, the Raiders are overwhelmingly excited to see their future. They feel like Mendoza is ready, thanks in part to the work he's done with veteran quarterback coach Mike Sullivan.

Prior to each play in practice, Mendoza calls the play for Sullivan away from the group, then goes through his footwork as if he's the quarterback, while Cousins took the first-team reps. It was mental reps, plus, for Mendoza.

During games, Sullivan and Mendoza stand 30 yards away from the play, with Mendoza practicing calling it, making the checks, and then watching how Cousins executed. What the Raiders smartly have is a personal tutor for their prized draft pick, and this has gone on since the spring.

"His command of the offense, his ability to articulate the huddle calls (and) communicate at the line of scrimmage, has improved consistently," Sullivan said. "It's certainly credit to him."

In addition, after each practice, Sullivan and Mendoza break down film of his performance on the scout team, and when there are miscues, he repeats it. Mendoza then studies the opponent's offense that he's been running just to learn.

While Cousins has taken nearly all of the first-team reps, the Raiders have snuck in some reps with the 1s for Mendoza. For instance, if the first team is working on their rushing offense on a Wednesday, Mendoza would get a snap or two just to mix him in. It rarely happened on passing plays, with Cousins taking all of those.

Now it's all Mendoza's turn, as the future is now for Las Vegas.

articles.headline: Sources: Vikings want to keep Kirk Cousins, talked to QB about staying in 2027
articles.description: The Vikings are interested in keeping Kirk Cousins as their QB next season, sources told NFL Network.
articles.body:
The Vikings brought in Kirk Cousins to help them this season, but they already are interested and have talked to the veteran quarterback about returning to Minnesota for the 2027 season, sources told NFL Network.

Before the Vikings completed their highly-anticipated blockbuster trade for Cousins on Tuesday, they had one more phone call to make. Team brass placed a call to agent Mike McCartney, who has represented Cousins for his entire career.

The message delivered in the short conversation was this: the Vikings would like for Cousins' return to Minnesota to be more than a one-year rental.

Cousins is set to be a free agent after this season, but if all goes well, don't be surprised if the sides find a way to stay together through 2027. The Vikings wanted to know if Cousins was open to talking about it -- and he was.

Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell officially announced Friday afternoon that Cousins would start for Minnesota, as expected, in Sunday's showdown against the division rival Green Bay Packers.

It has been a long and windy road at quarterback for the Vikings, who went from Cousins to Sam Darnold to J.J. McCarthy to Carson Wentz to Kyler Murray, only to go back to Wentz -- with a little Jaren Hall, Josh Dobbs, Nick Mullens and Max Brosmer mixed in.

Although Cousins is 38, he's playing as well as he has since his last season in Minnesota.

Cousins enters Sunday fifth in the NFL in passing yards (2,340) and second in touchdown passes (20), behind only Joe Burrow. He will be the first quarterback in NFL history to start back-to-back weeks for two different teams since quarterback starts became official in 1950, according to ESPN Research.

And at least for the near future, the Vikings would like to stop searching for a quarterback. When McCartney told general manager Nolan Teasley and executive vice president of football operations Rob Brzezinski that he believed Cousins was more than open to continuing the relationship into 2027 -- with no firm offers or deadlines -- the trade with the Las Vegas Raiders was on.

The Vikings took on Cousins' contract -- the rest of the minimum salary for 2026 -- but also the $10 million fully guaranteed in a roster bonus for 2027. If what both sides hope happens and Cousins becomes Minnesota's starter next season, that $10 million will be baked into his salary that is sure to exceed that number.

articles.headline: Steelers-Bengals odds, analysis, betting tips and recommended props
articles.description: Odds, analysis and picks to help you bet Sunday's Pittsburgh Steelers-Cincinnati Bengals game.
articles.body:
In the Week 3 matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals, a 30-27 Pittsburgh Steelers win at home, Jaylen Warren produced 176 total yards on 20 touches and Aaron Rodgers threw for 292 yards and three touchdowns, completing five passes of 20 or more yards.

However, this Steelers' pass game has lacked rhythm over the last two games, as Rodgers threw for less than 215 yards in both while completing only 58.2% of his attempts. This is a team that has been reliant on Warren (two straight games with over 100 yards rushing) and the rushing attack, as well as a top-10 defense allowing only 18.0 PPG (tied for fourth fewest in the league). But Rodgers and the Steelers will need to create some explosive plays through the air to match the Bengals. Let's see if they made some adjustments/corrections off the bye week.

Based on the numbers and the game tape, Joe Burrow is currently playing the best football in the league at the quarterback position. Over his last five games, Burrow is averaging 328.6 yards passing and completing over 75% of his throws, tossing 17 touchdown passes over that stretch. Timing, location, pocket mobility ... it's all there. And Burrow has an elite combination of receivers in Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Multi-level route runners and high-end matchup targets.

However, the Bengals' run game with Chase Brown is still looking for a way to create efficiency, and the defense, while creating splash plays, is giving up 354.9 yards per game (eighth most).

Betting outlook

I would stay with the trends when betting this game. That means taking the safe plays on Burrow with yards and completions, as I do see the Bengals rolling with a pass-heavy script.

Cincy isn't generating consistent production on the ground (85.6 yards per game), and the Steelers are allowing only 3.6 YPC. Throw the ball here to stay ahead of the sticks.

I like Warren as a dual-threat option, which allows me to bet his rushing + receiving total, but I'm going to stay lower on Rodgers in this one. The Steelers have been winning with an old-school identity, and it allows them to control tempo.

articles.headline: Ranking the top 10 Super Bowl performances by a defender
articles.description: Not all Super Bowl MVPs were quarterbacks or offensive stars. We listed 10 standout individual defensive performances.
articles.body:
Super Bowls are mostly remembered for offensive fireworks, miraculous fourth-quarter drives, gravity-defying catches and MVP quarterbacks who hoist the Vince Lombardi Trophy in victory.

Yet, as the old adage in football reminds us, offense sells tickets while defense wins championships.

While team defenses such as the 1985 Chicago Bears, 2000 Baltimore Ravens and 2013 Seattle Seahawks dominated as collective units, a select group of defenders delivered singular, dominant, game-altering performances on the NFL's biggest stage.

Here are 10 of the best individual defensive performances in Super Bowl history, including four defenders who earned the game's Most Valuable Player award.

COUNTDOWN TO SUPER BOWL LXI: ESPN will televise the Super Bowl for the first time in February. We are counting down to the big game with a Super Bowl Top 10 series, featuring rankings on everything from best catches and performances to biggest upsets, which will run every other Sunday leading up to Super Bowl LXI on Feb. 14, 2027.

1. Denver Broncos OLB Von Miller in Super Bowl 50

When: Feb. 7, 2016

Score: Broncos 24, Panthers 10

Stats: 2.5 sacks, 2 forced fumbles, 1 pass defended

Miller set the tone with a strip-sack of Cam Newton in the first quarter that was recovered in the end zone for a touchdown to give the Broncos a 10-0 lead. With Denver up 16-10 late in the fourth quarter, Miller once again jarred the ball loose from Newton when he sacked the quarterback deep in Carolina territory to put the Broncos in position to score the game-sealing touchdown four plays later.

Miller's performance was so dominant he earned unanimous Super Bowl MVP honors, becoming the 10th defensive player and fourth linebacker in NFL history to win the award.

2. Oakland Raiders LB Rod Martin in Super Bowl XV

When: Jan. 25, 1981

Score: Raiders 27, Eagles 10

Stats: 3 interceptions, 5 tackles

Martin created the standard for ball-hawking dominance on the biggest stage when he set the Super Bowl record for interceptions -- a record that is shared but still stands -- by picking off Ron Jaworski three times.

The linebacker staved off any chance of a Philadelphia comeback when he intercepted Jaworski in the first, third and fourth quarters of the Raiders' eventual 17-point win. He also added five tackles in Oakland's second Super Bowl victory.

3. Chicago Bears DE Richard Dent in Super Bowl XX

When: Jan. 26, 1986

Score: Bears 46, Patriots 10

Stats: 1.5 sacks, 2 forced fumbles, 1 blocked pass, 3 tackles

The "Sack Man" in Chicago's legendary "46 defense" led the NFL with 17.5 sacks during the 1985 season and gave a master class in pass rushing during Super Bowl XX. Dent wreaked havoc in the backfield with 1.5 sacks, three tackles two forced fumbles while constantly ripping through blocks to keep Patriots quarterback Tony Eason under pressure.

Dent earned Super Bowl MVP honors and is the last true defensive end to win the award.

4. Green Bay Packers DE Reggie White in Super Bowl X

articles.headline: Every Manchester United player, manager, executive since Glazers' takeover: Where are they now?
articles.description: The Glazer family took over Manchester United in 2005, but what has happened to the players, managers and executive staff since?
articles.body:
Manchester United have shuffled from one crisis to another since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013 after winning his 13th Premier League title.

The club were taken over in 2005 by American billionaires the Glazer family, but things have steadily unraveled under their leadership over the past 21 years and this season United have had their worst start to a Premier League season -- they sit just one point off the bottom of the table, having won once in 10 league games.

The finger of blame for United's woes has been pointed in many directions over the past decade or so, with the current hierarchy -- led by co-chairman Joel Glazer, minority owner Jim Ratcliffe, CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox -- taking plenty of flak for the recent malaise.

But a lot of different backroom senior staff have been involved in the club since 2005, a lot of different managers have tried and failed, and a lot of players have come and gone. So where are they now?

Jump to: Backroom staff | Managers | Incoming players

Backroom staff

David Gill (CEO)

Gill left his role in the summer of 2013 and worked as vice president of UEFA and FIFA, as well as serving as a vice-chairman of the English Football Association. Still a Man United board member, Gill stepped down from his role on the UEFA executive committee in 2025 and was named the chair at Telix Pharmaceuticals in September 2026.

Ed Woodward (executive vice-chairman)

Having advised the Glazer family during the takeover of Manchester United, Woodward was hired in 2005 and given charge of the commercial and media operations two years later. He replaced Gill as CEO in 2013 and left the club in February 2022.

Now, he is the co-owner of the Quinta da Pedra Alta vineyard in Portugal. He is also a partner at AGILIS Sports Advisory Group -- a London-based mergers and acquisitions boutique focused on the sports sector -- a trustee at the Bloomsbury Football Foundation, and a non-exec board member at Sentient Sports, which describes itself as "pioneering AI-driven athlete protection and sports innovation."

Matt Judge (director of football negotiations)

The former investment banker joined the club in 2012 and was involved in United's transfer business from 2014. He led contract negotiations under Woodward from 2016, but he took up a new role in March 2021 when Darren Fletcher was named technical director and John Murtough was promoted to football director before leaving in 2022. He is now a partner, alongside Woodward, at the aforementioned AGILIS Sports Advisory Group.

Dan Ashworth (sporting director)

Ashworth was named the FA's director of elite development in 2012. He moved to Brighton to become the club's technical director in 2019, before joining Newcastle United as sporting director in 2022. Portland Trail Blazers (9-3, fourth in the Western Conference) vs. Minnesota Timberwolves (9-4, fifth in the Western Conference)


              Minneapolis; Monday, 8 p.m. EST


              BOTTOM LINE: Portland will attempt to build upon its three-game win streak with a victory over Minnesota.


              The Timberwolves are 5-2 against Western Conference opponents. Minnesota is the Western Conference leader with 13.8 offensive rebounds per game led by Rudy Gobert averaging 3.8.


              The Trail Blazers are 9-3 against Western Conference opponents. Portland averages 119.6 points and has outscored opponents by 7.8 points per game.


              The 118.3 points per game the Timberwolves score are 6.5 more points than the Trail Blazers give up (111.8). The Trail Blazers are shooting 46.9% from the field, 3.5% higher than the 43.4% the Timberwolves' opponents have shot this season.


              TOP PERFORMERS: LaMelo Ball is scoring 18.6 points per game with 3.6 rebounds and 6.2 assists for the Timberwolves. Ayo Dosunmu is averaging 20.2 points and 4.5 rebounds while shooting 53.4% over the past 10 games.


              Deni Avdija is averaging 23.9 points, 6.1 rebounds and 6.3 assists for the Trail Blazers. Damian Lillard is averaging 2.9 made 3-pointers over the last 10 games.


              LAST 10 GAMES: Timberwolves: 6-4, averaging 117.5 points, 46.8 rebounds, 25.9 assists, 8.8 steals and 5.3 blocks per game while shooting 47.6% from the field. Their opponents have averaged 109.5 points per game.


              Trail Blazers: 7-3, averaging 118.3 points, 43.0 rebounds, 24.2 assists, 6.5 steals and 5.5 blocks per game while shooting 46.7% from the field. Their opponents have averaged 113.9 points.

articles.headline: 'Extremely lucky' Declan Rice hints new Arsenal contract will be signed soon
articles.description: Declan Rice has hinted he is likely to sign a new contract at Arsenal to extend his stay at the club beyond 2028.
articles.headlineJa: 「非常に幸運だ」デクラン・ライス、アーセナルとの新契約締結が間近であることを示唆
articles.descriptionJa: デクラン・ライスは、アーセナルでの残留期間を2028年以降に延長するため、クラブと新たな契約を締結する可能性が高いことを示唆した。
articles.body:
MADRID -- Declan Rice has hinted he is likely to sign a new contract at Arsenal to extend his stay at the club beyond 2028.

The 27-year-old joined the Gunners from West Ham for £105 million in 2023 and his current deal expires at the end of next season, although the club have an option to extend by a further year.

- Tuchel plays down racism row ahead of England's clash in Spain

- England have come a long way since World Cup heartbreak. But are they ready for Spain?

- What do England need vs. Spain, why does it matter, and who's next? 

Sources have told ESPN that talks have taken place across several months and Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta has said it is "a matter of time" before Rice commits his future to the club.

The midfielder expressed his desire to stay at the Premier League champions when addressing media ahead of England's Nations League clash with Spain in Madrid.

"I've been extremely lucky that I've managed to play at such a consistent level throughout my career," said Rice.

"I'm a player that always sets myself targets, always pushes for more. I've always been stable in the clubs I'm at. New contract hopefully on the horizon soon.

"I'm extremely lucky I'm at a club like Arsenal where the manager shows me so much trust, I've so many teammates who put so much energy and effort into me. I'm extremely lucky that I don't have to worry about that stuff. It makes playing football a lot easier."

Rice hopes England can emulate Arsenal's recent progress in overcoming years of underachievement to win the Premier League for the first time in 22 years and reaching last season's Champions League Final for only the second time in the club's history.

"What the manager has installed in us at Arsenal is to not have any fear," Rice said. "The progression in the Champions League over the last three years -- quarterfinal, semifinal, final -- coming to this stadium last year, we've been to the Bernabeu, Bayern Munich.

"The Arsenal of old may have struggled in those stadiums. Playing in that team now, putting on that shirt before that game, you know what you're going to get before you go out there.

"You're going to get a strong team, togetherness, we're going to run for each other, we're going to play forward, So I'm extremely lucky at the minute that I'm in a beautiful team with such great players and with a manager who is leading us and with players who listen to him and follows all his instructions. It is no surprise we're on the trajectory we're on at the minute. Long may it continue.

"That togetherness, that's what's building [with England]. Thomas is only short into his reign here at England. He's come in with the World Cup straight away and now playing the top teams in the Nations League.

articles.body:
Manchester United are monitoring Como superstar Nico Paz ahead of a move next summer, while Chelsea are considering a January swoop for Barcelona defender Jules Koundé. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United are monitoring Como superstar Nico Paz ahead of a move next summer, according to The Sun. The 22-year-old was already on United's radar before scoring twice and providing an assist against them in the UEFA Champions League last month. Mauricio Pochettino's arrival as manager could help their pursuit of his fellow Argentine, although Real Madrid retain an €80 million option to re-sign the midfielder in 2027. Meanwhile, The Telegraph says that Pochettino is expected to be backed in the January transfer window, with the Red Devils likely to be in the market for a defender and a striker.

- Chelsea are considering a January swoop for Barcelona defender Jules Koundé as a potential replacement for Malo Gusto, as per TEAMtalk. Barca are open to the 28-year-old's departure as they seek to raise funds for their own transfer plans, while Chelsea have been assessing the feasibility of any future deal. Despite interest from Saudi Arabia, Koundé would prefer to remain in Europe, with the Premier League his priority. A move to London is also understood to appeal to the France international.

- Liverpool and Bayern Munich are monitoring Stuttgart defender Finn Jeltsch, according to Christian Falk. Liverpool scouts have recently watched the 20-year-old, who is also on the radar of several other Premier League clubs. His ability to operate at both center back and right back has helped him earn a place in Germany's squad. However, Falk believes a move to England is unlikely to be Jeltsch's next step as he looks to progress gradually.

- Real Madrid are monitoring Atlético Mineiro center back Vitão, with Brighton and Everton also interested, Sport reports. Brighton are expected to make the first formal approach for the 18-year-old in January, with a proposed €14 million offer falling below his €20 million release clause for overseas clubs. Atlético Mineiro have attempted to extend the Brazilian's contract to increase that clause, but negotiations have stalled in recent weeks.

- Bayer Leverkusen are in advanced negotiations with attacking midfielder Ibrahim Maza over a new contract until 2031, Sky Germany has revealed. The proposed agreement contains no release clause, while his annual salary would rise from approximately €2.5 million gross to around €4 million plus bonuses. This development follows weeks of intense speculation surrounding Maza's future, who has been heavily linked with a move to Paris Saint-Germain in January.

articles.headline: Mauricio Pochettino to Man United: Is Tottenham love affair finally over?
articles.description: Mauricio Pochettino is back in the Premier League as the new Man United boss. For Tottenham fans, it's complicated.
articles.headlineJa: マウリシオ・ポチェッティーノがマンUへ：トッテナムとの愛の物語はついに終わるのか？
articles.descriptionJa: マウリシオ・ポチェッティーノがマンチェスター・ユナイテッドの新監督としてプレミアリーグに復帰します。トッテナムのファンにとっては、複雑な心境となるでしょう。
articles.body:
"He's magic, you know, Mauricio Pochettino!" For five years, these were the words that rang out amongst Tottenham fans.

First, at the old White Hart Lane -- a much-loved, if dilapidated, ground that became a fortress during Pochettino's years as head coach of the club. Then, at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium -- a magnificent arena that, in recent years, has felt more like a house of horrors than any sort of stronghold.

But now Pochettino is back in the Premier League, this time as Manchester United manager. And for Tottenham fans who once dreamed of seeing the Argentine return to north London, it's another reminder that the man who gave us so many unforgettable memories might never be coming home.

The Pochettino love affair

The Argentine manager joined Tottenham in 2014 and was at the helm of one of the best, and most beloved, Spurs teams in the club's history. Under Pochettino, Harry Kane (now a Ballon d'Or winner!), Son Heung-Min, Christian Eriksen, Dele Alli, Jan Vertonghen, Toby Alderweireld, Mousa Dembélé and Hugo Lloris all shone in ways that few football fans and pundits expected.

During the Pochettino era, Tottenham came agonisingly close to winning the Premier League and reached the Champions League final. They went an entire season unbeaten at home -- somewhat unthinkable now given the team's struggles at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium -- and played some of the most thrilling football in the league at the time.

There were famous victories over arch-rivals Arsenal and in Europe, including over Real Madrid and Borussia Dortmund, and, of course, there was that night in Amsterdam. When Lucas Moura scored an astonishing hat trick against Ajax to send Spurs to the Champions League final for the first time in our history.

For many Spurs fans, including myself, the Poch years brought some of our best ever memories of supporting the club. There was a special connection between Pochettino and fans. He was revered and many of us hoped that it would last forever -- even if we all knew that, really, nothing ever lasts that long. Especially not in football.

When Pochettino was sacked, rather unceremoniously, in November 2019 -- just months after taking us to the Champions League final -- it felt somewhat unjust.

It was clear for anyone to see in 2019 that Tottenham's squad was beginning to get stale in a number of areas and that what the club truly needed was a rebuild. For myriad reasons, that never came to fruition and so, when, results on the pitch took a nosedive in the winter of that year the axe fell on Pochettino.

Overnight, the man who had turned Tottenham into a truly formidable side capable of beating anyone on their day was gone. Since then, it's fair to say that no other manager that has taken the wheel at the club has managed to form the same sort of bond that Pochettino had with us.

Many have come and gone but it hasn't yet felt like any of them have "got" us the way that Pochettino did. It is early days under Roberto De Zerbi
